exposure: gestational age at repeat CS (<39 weeks vs. >=39 weeks)
type of repeat CS (elective vs. emergency)
outcome: incidence of emergency repeat cesarean section (EmRCS)
cohort: The study included 1421 women who underwent repeat cesarean sections at King Hamad University Hospital, Bahrain, from 2017 to 2021.
finding: Elective repeat cesarean sections (ERCS) scheduled at 39 weeks or later appear to reduce the risk of neonatal respiratory complications and NICU admission compared to those performed before 39 weeks.
mod_finding: The risk of spontaneous labor leading to emergency repeat procedures remains a concern, particularly among women with multiple previous CSs, despite the benefits of scheduled ERCS at 39 weeks for neonatal outcomes.
